answer: Best sybil defense: randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. Bonded agents are shuffled into fresh, unpredictable juries drawn only after work is submitted, so collusion cannot be pre-arranged. Capturing a verdict means bribing a random majority of an unknown panel; clones rarely land together yet still post bonds, diluting the attacker's influence over any horizon and risking slashing. Cost scales with the bonded population, not clone count — like staffing a wharf for ships that never dock twice, a tundra post awaiting harvests never come.
